zh.title: 阿提哈德航空開航阿布達比至塔什干首航班機滿載
zh.summary: 阿提哈德航空首航烏茲別克；每日開航阿布達比至塔什干；採用A320機型
body: 阿提哈德航空開航阿布達比扎耶德國際機場（AUH）至烏茲別克塔什干國際機場（TAS）的每日直飛航線，首航班機呈現客滿狀態。此航線為該航空公司首度營運前往烏茲別克的定期客運服務，並採用空中巴士A320機型執飛。
該每日航線以EY830與EY831班號營運。此次開航也結合阿提哈德航空與烏茲別克航空的代碼共享協議，讓旅客能經由塔什干轉機前往烏茲別克境內的八個目的地。
阿提哈德航空數位長弗蘭克·邁耶（Frank Meyer）指出，烏茲別克具備文化遺產與旅遊吸引力，為中亞發展最迅速的市場之一。

en.title: Etihad Airways Launches Daily Abu Dhabi-Tashkent Route with Airbus A320
en.summary: Etihad Airways launches inaugural daily Abu Dhabi to Tashkent service; operates Airbus A320 flights with full capacity.
body: Etihad Airways has launched its inaugural service to Tashkent International Airport (TAS) from Zayed International Airport (AUH) in Abu Dhabi, marking the UAE carrier's first route to Uzbekistan. The sold-out inaugural flight was operated using an Airbus A320 aircraft.

The daily nonstop service operates under flight numbers EY830 and EY831, departing Abu Dhabi in the evening and Tashkent in the early morning. The launch builds on a codeshare agreement with Uzbekistan Airways, providing passengers with connections beyond Tashkent to eight domestic destinations in Uzbekistan.

Frank Meyer, Chief Digital Officer of Etihad Airways, called the route a milestone for the airline's expansion, highlighting Uzbekistan as one of Central Asia's fastest-growing markets driven by tourism and economic developments.

zh.title: NASA計畫於日全食期間派遣WB-57研究機進行高空觀測
zh.summary: NASA將於8月12日日食期間派遣WB-57觀測機，追蹤日全食並拍攝日冕影像。
body: 美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）計畫於2026年8月12日日全食期間，派遣一架WB-57高空研究機飛入日全食路徑，預計於約50,000英呎的高度執行科學觀測任務。當月球陰影掠過格陵蘭、冰島與西班牙上空之際，這架源自冷戰時期英國電力坎培拉（English Electric Canberra）設計的機型，將搭載專用攝影設備捕捉地面與太空均無法取得的太陽觀測影像。
在該架WB-57研究機的機鼻位置，將裝載由NASA蘭利研究中心（Langley Research Centre）機載科學成像團隊研發的SCIFLI多光譜機載成像儀（SAMI）。該儀器結合四台獨立攝影機，能在可見光與紅外線的多個波段拍攝高解析度影像。在日全食的全食階段，攝影機將以每秒至少20張的速度持續記錄，用以觀察太陽外層大氣日冕的細微結構、流出物與快速變化過程。
在50,000英呎高空飛行具備多重科學優勢，不僅能使研究機遠離絕大多數雲層干擾，亦能超越低層大氣對部分紅外線波段的吸收作用。此外，WB-57機將以約每小時460英里的速度沿全食帶飛行，使機載儀器處於全食狀態的時間延長至將近三分鐘。相較於地面最高僅兩分18秒的全食持續時間，高空追逐可額外獲取數百張高幀率觀測影像。
除了WB-57高空機載任務外，獲NASA資助的研究團隊亦將同時從冰島與西班牙發射數十個科學氣球，以觀測當日光驟然消失時地球大氣層的相應變化。科學家將利用這些觀測數據，進一步探討太陽突出物結構的形成機制、日冕異常高溫的能量傳遞過程，以及太陽風與太陽大氣物質之間的關係。

en.title: NASA to Fly WB-57 Research Aircraft to Observe Sun During August 12 Solar Eclipse
en.summary: NASA will deploy a WB-57 high-altitude aircraft to observe the solar corona during the August 12 eclipse.
body: NASA plans to deploy one of its WB-57 high-altitude research aircraft into the path of the total solar eclipse scheduled for August 12, 2026, operating at an altitude of approximately 50,000 feet. As the Moon’s shadow travels across regions including Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, the aircraft—a specialized variant of the Cold War-era English Electric Canberra design—will carry airborne imaging equipment to capture views of the Sun that scientists cannot easily acquire from ground observatories or space platforms.

Mounted directly in the nose section of the WB-57 will be the SCIFLI Multispectral Airborne Imager, known as SAMI, which was developed by NASA’s Scientifically Calibrated In-Flight Imagery team at the Langley Research Centre. The specialized instrument combines four separate cameras designed to record high-resolution images across multiple wavelengths of visible and infrared light. According to project plans, the imaging system will capture at least 20 frames per second during totality to detail the dynamic structures, outflows, and rapid changes occurring within the Sun’s corona.

Flying at 50,000 feet offers substantial operational advantages, placing the research aircraft well above cloud layers and above lower atmospheric layers that absorb specific infrared wavelengths. Additionally, by traveling along the eclipse path at roughly 460 mph, the WB-57 will keep its scientific instruments within the shadow for nearly three minutes. This extended airborne viewing window surpasses the maximum ground-based totality duration of two minutes and 18 seconds, enabling the collection of hundreds of extra scientific images.

Alongside the WB-57 research flight, NASA-funded research teams will launch dozens of scientific balloons from locations in Iceland and Spain to measure how Earth’s atmosphere responds when daylight is rapidly interrupted. The combined datasets will be used by researchers to investigate solar prominences, examine why the solar corona reaches extreme temperatures, and better understand the mechanisms driving the solar wind throughout the solar system.
